texts.li: {A_nameDef} dragged in after a long shift and found {X_definite} waiting by the door, exactly where {X_pronoun} waits every evening, whether anyone comes home or not.
Nobody thanked {A_nameDef} for the day's work. Then {X_definite} heard {A_possessive} footsteps and nearly fell over with joy, which covered most of it.
{A_nameDef} sat down on the step, too tired to unlace {A_possessive} boots, and {X_definite} leaned {X_possessive} whole weight against {A_objective} until the worst of the day had drained off.
{A_nameDef} woke up pinned under the blankets by {X_definite}, who had climbed onto the bed sometime in the night and could not be argued off it.
Every night {X_definite} turns three slow circles and drops across {A_nameDef}'s feet. {A_nameDef} hasn't had warm toes this reliably in years.
{A_nameDef} claims to sleep better with {X_definite} snoring at the foot of the bed. The people in the next room have asked to see some proof.
{A_nameDef} looked away for one breath and the best piece left {A_possessive} plate. Across the room, {X_definite} was chewing and refusing all eye contact.
{A_nameDef} set {A_possessive} bowl down to scratch an itch. When {A_pronoun} looked back, {X_definite} had {X_possessive} whole face in it.
Half of {A_nameDef}'s dinner went out the door with {X_definite}. {A_nameDef} gave chase for three steps, then sat back down and ate the other half faster.
{A_nameDef} found a dead rat laid out on {A_possessive} pillow, neat as a place setting and still warm, with {X_definite} beside it waiting to be told how clever {X_pronoun} was.
A gift from {X_definite}: the back half of something small, left in {A_nameDef}'s boot. {A_nameDef} said thank you, because what else do you say?
{A_nameDef} praised {X_definite} once for a dead squirrel on the doorstep. Now there is a dead something on the doorstep every single morning.
{A_nameDef} spent the afternoon teaching {X_definite} to sit on command. By sunset {X_pronoun} sat on command about half the time, which {A_nameDef} is calling a triumph.
After a week of patience and stolen scraps, {X_definite} finally comes when {A_nameDef} whistles. Also when anyone whistles. Also at mealtimes, unwhistled for.
{A_nameDef} has taught {X_definite} to fetch. So far {X_pronoun} fetches the stick, chews the stick and buries the stick, in that order, every time.

{A_nameDef} sat alone behind the storehouse with {A_possessive} head in {A_possessive} hands. After a while {X_definite} came and leaned against {A_objective}, asking for nothing, which was exactly right.
Nobody else noticed that {A_nameDef} had gone quiet for days, but {X_definite} did, and has not left {A_possessive} side since.
{A_nameDef} cried for the first time in weeks, out by the pens, into the warm side of {X_definite}. Neither of them has mentioned it to anyone.
{A_nameDef} skipped supper and lay facing the wall. Some time later {X_definite} pushed the door open with {X_possessive} head and lay down beside the bed with a heavy sigh.
{A_nameDef} came back to find {A_possessive} spare boots reduced to a damp heap of leather, and {X_definite} asleep on the heap, worn out from the effort.
Something got at {A_nameDef}'s bedroll overnight and went straight through the middle. The evidence points, as it always does, to {X_definite}.
{A_nameDef} spent a week carving a decent spoon, and {X_definite} spent about a minute turning it back into kindling.
{A_nameDef} opened the storeroom and found {X_definite} sitting in the ruin of a sack of vegetables, very round and not the least bit sorry.
Somebody left the larder door open. By the time {A_nameDef} noticed, {X_definite} had eaten a respectable share of the raw stores and was working on the rest.
{A_nameDef} followed a trail of gnawed peel from the storeroom to the barn, where {X_definite} lay on {X_possessive} side, groaning, and deserving every bit of it.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a child at play with an animal

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {X_definite} spent the whole afternoon chasing each other round the yard. By the end, nobody could tell who was chasing whom.
{A_nameDef} tied a ribbon on {X_definite} and declared {X_objective} a knight of the colony, with full honors. The knight ate the ribbon.
{A_nameDef} built {X_definite} a little house out of sticks and an old blanket. It stood proudly until {X_definite} tried to go inside.
{A_nameDef} is teaching {X_definite} to count, by holding up fingers and waiting for an answer. So far the only one learning anything is {A_nameDef}, and it's patience.
On paper, {X_definite} isn't {A_nameDef}'s animal. Lately, though, {X_pronoun} follows {A_nameDef} from room to room and sleeps across {A_possessive} doorway.

{A_nameDef} never fed {X_definite}, never trained {X_objective}, never so much as scratched {X_possessive} ears. None of that matters, apparently: {X_definite} now waits under {A_possessive} chair at every meal.
Nobody can work out why {X_definite} picked {A_nameDef}, least of all {A_nameDef}, who has been escorted to the latrine and back twice today.
{A_nameDef} was overheard in the pens, telling {X_definite} everything that has gone wrong this season, in order. The animal listened to all of it and asked only for a scratch.
{A_nameDef} talks to {X_definite} at night about the things {A_pronoun} won't say at the table. So far, the secrets are safe.
{A_nameDef} asked {X_definite} whether {A_pronoun} was doing a good job out here, and got a long yawn in reply. {A_nameDef} has decided to take that as a yes.
Everyone in the colony can walk past {X_definite} in peace except {A_nameDef}, who gets a long, flat, unblinking stare every single time.
{A_nameDef} has tried scraps, soft words and a respectful distance. None of it has worked on {X_definite}, who still goes for {A_possessive} ankles on sight.
{A_nameDef} swears {X_definite} lies in wait behind the barn door for {A_objective} and nobody else. Nobody believed it until they saw it happen twice before breakfast.
Every morning {X_definite} follows {A_nameDef} out to work, lies down just out of the way, and supervises. The work goes no faster. {A_nameDef} is in a far better mood.
{A_nameDef} tried to leave {X_definite} shut in today and found {X_objective} at the work site half an hour later, very pleased about it. Nobody knows how.
{A_nameDef} spent the day hauling with {X_definite} at {A_possessive} heels, carrying nothing, underfoot at every turn, and plainly having the best day of {X_possessive} life.
This morning it took {X_definite} a long time to get up, and longer to manage the step. {A_nameDef} waited at the bottom and didn't say a word.
{A_nameDef} noticed today that {X_definite} walks to meet {A_objective} now instead of running. It's still every day. That part hasn't changed.
{A_nameDef} moved {X_definite}'s sleeping spot closer to the fire and says it's because of the draft. Nobody believes that, and nobody says so.
{A_nameDef} found a heap of tiny, squalling newborns in the straw this morning, with {X_definite} standing over them like an anxious relative who wants no visitors.
There are new mouths in the barn. {A_nameDef} tried to count them under the hard stare of {X_definite}, lost track because they kept moving, and came in grinning.
{A_nameDef} spent half the evening in the barn naming the newborns after members of the council, while {X_definite} dozed beside the pile. The runt got the loudest councilor's name.
A traveler reached out to clap {A_nameDef} on the shoulder and found {X_definite} suddenly in the way, very still, very attentive. The traveler kept their hands to themselves after that.
{A_nameDef} never asked {X_definite} to guard {A_objective}. But whenever a stranger comes near, there {X_pronoun} is, standing just in front of {A_nameDef}, as if by accident.
Words got sharp between {A_nameDef} and an outsider at the gate, and before the second sentence {X_definite} was planted between them, silent, eyes fixed on the stranger.
Well after dark, {X_definite} started making an unholy noise at nothing, and kept at it until {A_nameDef} went out in a blanket to sit with {X_objective}.
{A_nameDef} is awake because {X_definite} is awake, and {X_definite} is awake because of something past the wall that nobody else can see.
{A_nameDef} lay listening to {X_definite} cry out toward the tree line, over and over, and tried very hard not to wonder what {X_pronoun} was crying at.
Work stopped all over the colony when {X_indefinite} crossed the far meadow, slow and enormous. {A_nameDef} saw {X_objective} first and has not stopped talking about it.
{A_nameDef} looked up from {A_possessive} work and there was {X_indefinite} at the edge of the trees, looking back. Neither moved for a long moment. Then {X_pronoun} was simply gone.
{A_nameDef} watched {X_definite} drink from the stream for the better part of an hour and came back with nothing done and no apology whatsoever.
{A_nameDef} crept closer to {X_definite} than anyone has dared, close enough to hear {X_objective} breathe, and came back trembling, with the look of someone who has made a decision.
{A_nameDef} lay flat in the grass most of the afternoon, studying {X_definite}: how {X_pronoun} moved, where {X_pronoun} set {X_possessive} feet, what made {X_objective} lift {X_possessive} head.
{A_nameDef} has seen {X_indefinite} up close now, close enough to count the scars, and talks about nothing else. {A_nameDef} has also started pacing out a very large pen.
{A_nameDef} was first up this morning and found {X_indefinite} grazing in the mist past the fence. Neither of them moved for a long while. Then somebody slammed a door.
In the gray light before breakfast, {A_nameDef} watched {X_indefinite} step out of the trees, nose at the wet grass, and step back in. {A_nameDef} told nobody, as if telling would spend it.
{A_nameDef} stood very still at the well while {X_indefinite} drank from the runoff not ten paces away. The bucket grew heavy in {A_possessive} hands. {A_nameDef} didn't set it down.
{A_nameDef} gave up counting at forty: {X_indefinite} and all {X_possessive} kind, moving past the colony in a long, unhurried line that took most of the afternoon.
A herd went by to the south today, {X_definite} straggling at the back. {A_nameDef} stopped work to watch and was the last one back to it.
The ground hummed for an hour as the herd went past. {A_nameDef} stood at the edge of the fields with {A_possessive} mouth slightly open, like a child at a parade.
{A_nameDef} worked all morning to birdsong from the hedges, with {X_indefinite} dozing on a warm rock nearby. For a few hours the world seemed to have forgotten to be dangerous.
The hedges are full of song this time of year. {A_nameDef} ate lunch on an upturned bucket, watching {X_indefinite} poke through the new grass, and felt, briefly, like a person again.
{A_nameDef} whistled back at the birds for most of the afternoon. They ignored {A_objective}, but {X_indefinite} crept out of the grass to see what all the fuss was about.
Out past the fields {X_indefinite} called into the cold dark, and something farther off called back. {A_nameDef} checked the gate twice, and then once more.
{A_nameDef} lay awake listening to {X_indefinite} somewhere in the bare trees, calling and calling, and could not decide whether the sound was lonely or hungry.
The calling went on half the night. {A_nameDef} swears that at one point {X_indefinite} was right outside the fence, close enough to hear the breath between calls.
For most of the afternoon {X_indefinite} paced the far side of the fence, keeping exactly level with {A_nameDef} as {A_pronoun} worked. {A_nameDef} found a reason to finish early.
{A_nameDef} went out for firewood and came face to face with {X_indefinite} nosing at the woodpile. Both backed away slowly. Only one of them looked embarrassed about it.
There are fresh prints right up to the edge of the fields, and {X_indefinite} lying in the shade just past them, yawning, watching {A_nameDef} like someone taking measurements.
{A_nameDef} felt it before seeing it: {X_indefinite}, low in the long grass, eyes on {A_objective}. When {A_nameDef} stood up straight, the animal didn't run. That was the worst part.
{A_nameDef} walked out to the fields at first light and found a whole row of seedlings bitten off at the root, with {X_indefinite} at the end of the row, still chewing.
{A_nameDef} chased {X_indefinite} out of the crops three times before noon. The fourth time, {A_nameDef} sat down in the dirt and let {X_objective} have the corner.
{A_nameDef} has a new enemy: {X_indefinite} that lives under the hedge and eats exactly the plants {A_nameDef} cares about most, and nothing else.
{A_nameDef} has been leaving crusts on the same flat stone every day. Today {X_indefinite} was already waiting beside it, looking pointedly at {A_possessive} pocket.
{A_nameDef} held out a handful of grain and kept still for a very long time, and at the end of it {X_indefinite} ate out of {A_possessive} palm, then bolted.
{A_nameDef} has been sharing lunch with {X_indefinite} at the edge of the field all week. The gap between them shrinks a little every day. {A_nameDef} pretends not to notice.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a child meets a wild animal

texts.li: {A_nameDef} stood perfectly still in the long grass while {X_indefinite} came right up and sniffed {A_possessive} hair. {A_nameDef} has told everyone. Some people twice.
The adults saw {X_indefinite} wander toward {A_nameDef} and froze. {A_nameDef} didn't, and held out half an apple, and {X_definite} took it gently and wandered off again.
{A_nameDef} came running in out of breath: {X_indefinite} had touched noses with {A_objective} down by the water. There is now a drawing of it on the wall above {A_possessive} bed.
{A_nameDef} found prints by the water deep enough to hold rain and wide enough to stand in. Somewhere out there, {X_indefinite} is going about {X_possessive} business, and the business is enormous.

Snapped saplings, flattened brush, and tracks the size of serving platters lead toward the hills. {A_nameDef} followed them a hundred paces, glimpsed {X_indefinite} through the trees, and decided that was plenty.
{A_nameDef} laid a hand flat in one of {X_definite}'s footprints. Then the other hand beside it. There was still room left over, and {A_nameDef} came home rather quiet.
{A_nameDef} wanted to know what {X_indefinite} felt like up close, so {A_pronoun} walked straight up and laid a hand on {X_possessive} flank. Everyone watching stopped breathing.
On a dare, {A_nameDef} crept up behind {X_definite} and poked {X_objective} with a stick, then stood there just long enough to watch {X_possessive} head come round, very slowly.
{A_nameDef} tried to hand-feed {X_indefinite} a turnip. It isn't clear yet whether the colony will remember that as brave, or as the last thing {A_nameDef} ever did.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: the beast at the tree line

texts.li: {A_nameDef} saw {X_definite} at the tree line today, standing just where {X_pronoun} stood the day it all went wrong. They looked at each other until {X_pronoun} lost interest.
{A_nameDef} dropped a full bucket in the yard and didn't notice. Out past the fence, {X_definite} was pacing, unhurried, the way a thing paces once it has already won.
{A_nameDef} knew the shape at once, even at that distance: {X_definite}, back again, nosing along the edge of the trees as if the place belonged to {X_objective}.
{A_nameDef} spotted {X_definite} drinking at the far water and came back fast, without the water. Everyone here knows that name, and what goes with it.
Word went round the colony in minutes: {X_definite} has been seen again at the edge of the trees. {A_nameDef} was the one who spotted {X_objective}, and keeps checking over {A_possessive} shoulder.
{A_nameDef} has started carrying a blade to the latrine, ever since {X_definite} was seen circling the fields again in broad daylight.
{A_nameDef} set {A_possessive} hat down on a fence post for one moment, and {X_indefinite} made off with it into the brush. The hat has not been seen since.
{A_nameDef} chased {X_indefinite} halfway to the hills for a stolen glove, lost {X_objective} in a thicket, and came back with burrs, scratches and one glove.
{A_nameDef}'s lunch was wrapped, set aside, and then gone. A trail of crumbs led to {X_indefinite} under a bush, looking fat and unbothered.
{A_nameDef} was on {A_possessive} usual midnight walk when {X_indefinite} crossed the path ahead, pale in the starlight. They regarded each other like two people who keep the same hours.
While the rest of the colony slept, {A_nameDef} sat on the step and watched {X_indefinite} go about {X_possessive} night's business in the yard. Good company: quiet, and no talk of chores.
{A_nameDef} likes the colony best at night. Tonight {X_indefinite} came to the edge of the light to see who else was awake, and stayed a while.
{A_nameDef} watched {X_indefinite} and a rival go at each other in the meadow for the best part of an hour, heads down, churning the mud to soup. Neither won. Both limped off proud.
The whole colony could hear {X_definite} and a challenger colliding, over and over, out past the fields. {A_nameDef} went to watch and came back with opinions about technique.
{A_nameDef} bet a week of washing-up on {X_definite} against the bigger one, and lost, narrowly, in the mud. {A_nameDef} is demanding a rematch from the animals.
